reasoningSteps: Define a fictional checkout with three units at 12 credits each and a five-credit discount; the correct pure calculation is 3 × 12 − 5 = 31 credits, before any storage or interface behavior.
A unit test of calculateTotal isolates arithmetic and detects 30 or 36, but a green arithmetic test does not show that an API persists 31 or that a user can submit the order.
An integration test exercises the API-to-repository boundary with an isolated fake or test database; compare the stored amount with 31 rather than mocking away the very boundary under examination.

An end-to-end test starts at the checkout UI and verifies submission and displayed confirmation, including keyboard reachability; it observes user behavior but offers less precise failure localization.
For a mutation that changes the discount from five to six, predict the lowest layer that should fail first; for a disabled submit control, explain why a pure calculation test remains green.

Use The Practical Test Pyramid (https://martinfowler.com/articles/practical-test-pyramid.html) to distinguish a balance of granular feedback from the unsupported rule that every project needs fixed layer ratios.

reasoningSteps: Start from a wholly invented checkout trace: domain total 3100 cents, API JSON totalCents=3100, persistence record totalCents=31, and browser confirmation shows 0.31.
Notice that the pure calculation and API payload agree on 3100, so rewriting the arithmetic before checking the persistence adapter risks changing a working component.
State the expected persistence contract explicitly: totalCents must store an integer number of cents; storing 31 when the input is 3100 violates the contract by a factor of 100.
Use a narrow adapter integration test to compare the emitted 3100 with stored 31, then inspect the synthetic mapToRecord method for an accidental division by 100.
After removing the inappropriate conversion, rerun unit arithmetic, adapter persistence, and browser display expectations: 3100 cents should render as 31.00 credits.
Treat the trace as evidence for this fixture only: a real outage could involve formatting, stale data or cache, so avoid presenting the fictional diagnosis as a production incident.

Implement a mapToRecord(totalCents) fixture that incorrectly divides by 100 and assert the failing result 31 versus required 3100.
Add a narrow integration assertion against an in-memory repository; it should fail on the bad mapper before any browser or real database is involved.
Correct mapToRecord to preserve totalCents=3100 and assert the UI formatting function converts cents to the string '31.00' only at the presentation boundary.
